phases.title: Protect the code
phases.goal: Stop secrets, vulnerable code, and known-bad dependencies before they are merged. These checks are cheap to add and give results on day one.

phases.title: Secure the pipeline and the build
phases.goal: Treat the pipeline as production: lock down how jobs get credentials, what they build on, and what infrastructure they create.

phases.title: Ship artifacts you can trust
phases.goal: Know what is inside every release, sign it, and refuse anything unsigned or non-compliant at the cluster door.

phases.title: Test and watch what runs
phases.goal: Attack the running application, check built mobile apps, and keep an eye on cloud accounts and containers after deploy.

phases.title: Run it as a program
phases.goal: Collect every finding in one place, decide what blocks a release, design security in early, and measure maturity over time.

stages.title: Company baseline and ownership
stages.goal: Know which assets and data you protect, who owns them, and which vendors can access them.
stages.keywords: smb small company inventory assets vendors privacy retention evidence risk exceptions
acceptance: Inventory critical assets and sensitive data with an accountable owner.
Record vendor access, retention decisions and incident contacts.
Review dated evidence and risk exceptions; remove expired exceptions.

stages.title: Workforce and service identities
stages.goal: Require strong sign-in, constrain privileged access and revoke departed or compromised identities.
stages.keywords: sso mfa access offboarding joiner mover leaver oidc workload credentials recovery
acceptance: Test MFA, administrator recovery and offboarding across business services.
Record service identities, least privilege and short-lived credentials.
Verify active sessions are revoked separately from changing a password or key.

stages.title: SaaS and email security
stages.goal: Review business tenants, sharing, OAuth apps, forwarding and domain mail authentication.
stages.keywords: microsoft 365 google workspace email oauth forwarding spf dkim dmarc
acceptance: Assess only in-scope products using a reviewed read-access identity.
Review OAuth consent, external sharing, forwarding and privileged settings.
Test SPF, DKIM and DMARC separately; record unsupported and license-dependent checks.

stages.title: Backups and recovery
stages.goal: Restore a critical business service within its recorded recovery objectives.
stages.keywords: backup restore ransomware immutable offsite rpo rto disaster recovery
acceptance: Record scope, RPO/RTO, retention, backup owner and failure destination.

stages.title: External exposure, domains and TLS
stages.goal: Know your internet-facing services and retain control of their domains and management access.

acceptance: Inventory public services, DNS records, certificates and registrar owners.

stages.title: Pipeline security
stages.goal: Make sure the pipeline itself cannot be abused to steal secrets or push malicious builds.
stages.keywords: cicd pipeline gitlab-ci runners variables poisoned pipeline

builtins.text: Make the default GITHUB_TOKEN read-only, pin actions by commit SHA, require approval for workflows from forks, and use OIDC (permissions: id-token: write) instead of long-lived cloud keys.

Use protected branches and tags, protected and masked CI/CD variables, separate runners for protected branches, and id_tokens (OIDC) instead of long-lived cloud keys. Pipeline execution policies (Ultimate) can force security jobs into every project.

stages.title: Logging and alert delivery

stages.title: Incident response and rehearsal
stages.goal: Contain incidents, preserve evidence, recover service and track the follow-up work.
stages.keywords: incident response tabletop leak supply chain containment escalation forensic recovery
acceptance: Keep private contacts, escalation, containment authority and evidence storage current.
Exercise a credential leak or dependency compromise with synthetic evidence.
Measure containment/recovery, retest access and assign follow-up owners.

stages.title: API roles, tenants and business logic
stages.goal: Prove denied access has neither data disclosure nor side effects across users, roles and tenants.
stages.keywords: api authorization bola idor tenant rbac business logic access control
acceptance: Test anonymous, owner, other-user, other-tenant, reader/admin and revoked identities.
Include export, batch, nested-resource, asynchronous and alternate-method routes.
Assert response content and resulting state using real application fixtures.
